documents.title: OAI's Guidance for Fall 2024: AI & Academic Integrity
documents.stance_why: The deck says 'there is currently no AI policy that applies to the entire university system' and 'Faculty are responsible for determining what use of generative AI tools, if any, is appropriate in their courses'. It offers three templates, 'Strict / No-use Limited / Conditional Encouraging/ Open', so the stance is delegates with tiers.
documents.summary: Slide deck from the Assistant Dean for Academic Integrity explaining that AU has no university-wide AI policy and that faculty decide course AI use. It gives advice for writing course policies, three model tiers (strict, limited, open), and a flowchart for suspected misuse; faculty may not grade-penalize and must route concerns to OAI. OAI does not use AI detectors. Examples from other institutions are included but are not AU policy.

documents.summary: Short interim OIT guidance page stating AI use is not banned by the Academic Integrity Code and that there is no single university AI policy.
